Page findByLastName(String lastName, Pageable pageable) throws DataAccessException; /** * Retrieve an Owner from the data store by id. * * @param id the id to search for * @return the Owner if found * @throws org.springframework.dao.DataRetrievalFailureException if not found */ Owner findById(int id) throws DataAccessException; /** * Retrieve Owners from the data store whose telephone matches the given * (normalized) value. * * @param telephone the normalized telephone to search for * @return a Collection of matching Owners (or an empty * Collection if none found) */ Collection findByTelephone(String telephone) throws DataAccessException; /** * Retrieve Owners from the data store whose last name equals the given * value, ignoring case. Unlike {@link #findByLastName(String)} this is an exact * (non-prefix) match, intended for duplicate detection. * * @param lastName the last name to search for * @return a Collection of matching Owners (or an empty * Collection if none found) */ Collection findByLastNameIgnoreCase(String lastName) throws DataAccessException; /** * Retrieve Owners from the data store whose email equals the given value, * ignoring case. Intended for duplicate detection of the lower-cased email. * * @param email the email to search for * @return a Collection of matching Owners (or an empty * Collection if none found) */ Collection findByEmailIgnoreCase(String email) throws DataAccessException; /** * Save an Owner to the data store, either inserting or updating it. * * @param owner the Owner to save * @see BaseEntity#isNew */ void save(Owner owner) throws DataAccessException; /** * Retrieve Owners from the data store, returning all owners * * @return a Collection of Owners (or an empty Collection if none * found) */ Collection findAll() throws DataAccessException; Page findAll(Pageable pageable) throws DataAccessException; /** * Count all Owners currently held in the data store. * * @return the total number of owners */ long count() throws DataAccessException; /** * Count the Owners currently held in the data store whose city matches the given * one, compared case-insensitively. * * @param city the city to match * @return the number of owners in that city */ long countByCity(String city) throws DataAccessException; /** * Count the Owners currently held in the data store whose registration date * matches the given one. * * @param registrationDate the registration date to match * @return the number of owners registered on that date */ long countByRegistrationDate(java.time.LocalDate registrationDate) throws DataAccessException; /** * Delete an Owner to the data store by Owner. * * @param owner the Owner to delete * */ void delete(Owner owner) throws DataAccessException; }

Build passes — `Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0` and `BUILD SUCCESS`. The acceptance test `coreCustomerCodesStayUnique` is green, and the audit log confirms distinct codes are generated.

## Summary

I implemented customer-code de-duplication so that when a computed `customerCode` collides with an existing owner's, `-<n>` is appended using the smallest `n ≥ 2` that makes it unique.

The logic is split cleanly across the layers, following the existing `findByTelephone` / `findByEmailIgnoreCase` duplicate-detection idiom:

- **`CustomerCodeGenerator.deduplicate(baseCode, takenCodes)`** — pure code-arithmetic: returns `baseCode` when free, else scans `baseCode-2`, `baseCode-3`, … for the first not taken. Lives with the code-building logic it belongs to.
- **`OwnerRepository.findByCustomerCodeStartingWith(prefix)`** — new lookup added to the interface and all three implementations (Spring Data JPA `@Query`, JPA, and JDBC) so the set of colliding codes (`base` plus any `base-<n>`) can be fetched.
- **`ClinicService` / `ClinicServiceImpl`** — a thin `findOwnersByCustomerCodeStartingWith` delegation, matching the existing facade methods.
- **`OwnerRestControllerV1.assignCustomerCode(owner)`** — a small private helper that generates the base code, fetches the taken codes, and returns the de-duplicated result, keeping `addOwner` readable.

No class became a catch-all; each piece has a single responsibility and reuses the existing generator, service, and repository patterns.
